coverage: All 120 families run exhaustively (36,825 typed questions); 0 unsupported, 0 sampled. Every family has a reference in refs/number_a_1..4.py (shared helpers refs/number_a_common.py).
mutation_test: A copy of the data with every stored answer perturbed (numeric+1, next letter, dropped/reversed list items) was run against all 120 references: every family flags >=98% (all of them 100%) of the perturbed answers, 0 reference errors, so no reference is vacuous.
choice_options: Typed choice questions do not carry their option texts in $DATA. I exported only the `options` field of the 24 choice families with /tmp/certout/number-a/exportopts.ts (calls the production pool() to read item.options; no solving code is read or used) into /tmp/certout/number-a/opts/. A first probe of one aabig item also printed that item's metadata (steps/bugs); it was not used.
figure_as_statement: Where the figure is part of the question (blocks, grids, pictographs, ten frames, dots, tables, number lines) the answer is derived from the figure data and, wherever the prompt also states numbers, the figure is checked against the prompt (mismatch would be reported). acnlpos is the exception: the position of '?' exists only in the picture, so the reference derives the value from the word form of the same item (first stone + places x spacing) and requires the picture (axis start, step, ?) to agree; the rendering itself is not inspected.

judgement_references.aabig: object sizes ranked from common knowledge (litres of room); pairs closer than a factor 2 would be reported Ambiguous (none occurs).
judgement_references.aechk: reasonableness: reasonable if within 25% of both the exact value and the leading-digit estimate, far off if >=1.5x or <=2/3x of both (no question fell in between); 'needs an exact answer' uses a 16-item human classification; two items (chairs for 32 invited guests: 13 keyed questions, weight of gold at a jeweller: 16 keyed questions) are judgement calls classified as exact; product-size options accepted within a factor 2 of the exact product.
judgement_references.rounding: all rounding is half-up (ties go up), the school convention; no stored answer depended on the choice except where ties occur and all agreed.

form_checks: form=True (value and required form) used for achalf, agmix, agnl, agpfrac, agrupee (2 d.p.), aecmp; all passed.
mc_notes: Runner mcBad (value-equality) fires for agmix 248, agnl 25, agpfrac 160. agnl/agpfrac: the equal distractors are unreduced ('1 2/4', '25/100') while the prompt demands simplest form, so they are correct distractors; agmix: see register (low).
word_forms: 34,524 word forms were compared for answer equality with the typed form (0 differences). Wording was NOT verified generally; I read two word prompts per family (about 200) and found no mathematical problem (numbers, units and question matched the typed item). Automated number-multiset comparison of typed vs word prompts is not meaningful (stories re-describe the numbers).
property_scans: scan_props.py: the regrouping property named in each family title holds for every question (acsub2, acsub3, adcol3, addr, aecol4 need regrouping; acsubn, aeadd3, aeaddn form 0 do not; aeaddn totals <= 200). scan_fig.py: figure/prompt agreement for 15 further families. scan_opts.py: option text defects (only aaname:99).
statement_validity_checks: agfta stated prime factorisations (product and primality), aghlp stated HCF/LCM facts and existence of the partner number, admental stated shortcut decomposition, agptest 'none divides' premise (n prime), aghlw wording classification, adseq constant difference, ahsqd non-square, aiddiv/aidword exact division: all hold for every question.
